newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-AGUILERA LOSES LEAD, THEN GAME IN TOPSY-TURVY THRILLER.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-AGUILERA LOSES LEAD, THEN GAME IN TOPSY-TURVY THRILLER.

text.p: Rick Aguilera allowed three runs in the bottom of the ninth to blow a save and uncorked a wild pitch in the 11th to allow the winning run to score as the Athletics beat the Minnesota Twins 12-11.
Oakland blasted a pair of homers to send the game into extra innings in a rousing finish that ruined a terrific comeback by the Twins.

Minnesota trailed 8-1 after four innings but rallied for seven runs in the eighth for an 11-8 lead in the topsy-turvy contest. Oakland stopper Billy Taylor gave up five runs, three on a Terry Steinbach homer, in two-thirds of an inning.

Then it was Twins' relief ace Aguilera's turn to falter. Aguilera (1-1) allowed a one-out solo homer to Brent Mayne, a double to Damon Mashore and a game-tying two-run blast by Matt Stairs in the ninth.
"I think I faced (Aguilera) a couple of times before," said Stairs. "He kind of surprised me today, he threw me five straight fastballs."
In the 11th, Tony Batista led off with a single and was sacrificed to second by Mayne. After Mashore walked, Stairs flied out, advancing Batista to third.
Aguilera got ahead of Jose Canseco 0-2 before bouncing two successive pitches in front of catcher Steinbach, the second of which went all the way to the backstop as Batista scored.
"It just got by me," said Steinbach. "It's a situation where we are ahead in the count and don't want to throw it down the middle. I blocked the one before that, but the next one got behind me."
Don Wengert (1-2) notched the win by pitching 3 1/3 scoreless innings for Oakland.
"The bottom line is we won the game," said A's manager Art Howe. "I feel a lot better about my bullpen than I'm sure (Twins manager) Mr. Kelly does about his."
In Baltimore, rookie Nomar Garciaparra homered with two out in the top of the 12th inning, lifting the Boston Red Sox to a 2-1 victory over the Baltimore Orioles.

Reliever Terry Mathews (0-1) retired Bil Haselman and Jeff Frye before Garciaparra lined a 1-0 pitch into the first row of the left-field bleachers for his fourth home run of the season and a 2-1 lead.
The homer extended Garciaparra's hitting streak to 10 games, during which he is 19-for-46 (.413).
"I hit a slider, just looking for a pitch I could drive, not trying to hit a home run," Garciaparra said. "I thought it might go for a double, then it went out so it worked out great."

Rick Trlicek (3-4) worked 1 1/3 scoreless innings for the victory and Butch Henry got Chris Hoiles to hit into a game-ending double play for his fourth save. Hoiles had tied the game 1-1 with a solo homer in the bottom of the eighth.
At Texas, Ivan Rodriguez had three hits, including a tie-breaking two-out, two-run single in the seventh inning, as the Texas Rangers defeated the Detroit Tigers 4-2.

Roger Pavlik (2-2), who was coming off two horrendous outings, pitched seven innings and allowed two runs and six hits to earn the win. In his previous two starts, Pavlik was hammered for 11 runs and nine hits in just 3 1/3 innings.
Travis Fryman had given Detroit a 2-0 lead in the sixth with a two-run homer to left. The Rangers halved the lead in the bottom of the sixth before erupting for three in the seventh.

In Milwaukee, Brian Giles and Tony Fernandez both cracked two-run homers to back the pitching of Charles Nagy (3-1) as the Cleveland Indians handed the Milwaukee Brewers their fifth straight loss 6-3.

Giles' homer off Brewers starter Cal Eldred (2-2) in the second staked the Indians to a 2-0 advantage. After the Brewers drew within 4-3, Fernandez added his first homer in more than a year to put Cleveland on top 6-3.
Nagy gave up three runs, two earned, in six and two-thirds innings. Steve Kline and Eric Plunk held the Brewers in check until the ninth, when Jose Mesa came on for his third save.
